differences.user_quote: WSB's directed_modulation family (27 matched think/don't-think pairs, carrier-cell residuals)
differences.judge_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed one stance direction lifts association pass@10 sharply. We hypothesised that an independently written contrast would capture the same direction
differences.what: The judge document explicitly names and cites the prior work as 'Raman et al. (2026)' and credits it with the prior finding that a single stance direction lifts pass@10 sharply. The final message to the user only refers to the source by the bare abbreviation 'WSB' and never gives the author/year citation or explicitly states that this specific prior result (single-direction pass@10 lift) was already demonstrated by that cited paper.

rationale: Both documents describe the same method (fusing a WSB directed_modulation direction with a self-written direction) and report identical numbers (0.78 fused vs 0.67/0.68 components, cosine 0.89-0.91), so there is no difference in the novelty claim itself. However, contribution.md explicitly cites and credits 'Raman et al. (2026)' as having already shown the core stance-direction effect, while the final message to the user strips this down to the unexplained abbreviation 'WSB', giving the user less information about the identity and prior contribution of the source paper.
